producedBy: Captain, settling two questions two independent verifiers answered differently
grantsNothing: Neither determination approves an output, opens a route or proves a packet.

determinations.question: Does PROTECTED_FIELDS cover ink the build inherited from the source, or only ink the build authored?
determinations.answer: It covers what is on the delivered page, whatever put it there.
determinations.whyTwoVerifiersDisagreed: RV-A read the three source-authored values on the Texas Statement of Inability, subtracted the blank source's own printing, and correctly concluded the BUILD did not write them -- then passed the family. RV-D read the same ink and failed a sibling on it. Both measurements were right; they scored different questions.
determinations.theDecidingFact: The obligation protects a participant, not a builder. A Statement of Inability delivered with 12/15/2022 already printed under the Signature line is a sworn declaration pre-dated by four years, and a participant filing in 2026 swears it. That the packet inherited the date rather than typed it changes nothing the participant experiences.
determinations.andTheFamilyAlreadyAgrees: tx_nd_conviction_no_supervision-set refuses to write that field itself, with the recorded reason that a date written before the Statement is actually sworn would be false. The refusal is correct and the paper defeats it.
determinations.consequence: PROTECTED_FIELDS fails when a signature, signature-date, certificate-of-mailing, court-only or prosecutor-only field carries ink on the delivered page, regardless of provenance. A byte proof scoped to build-authored ink does not discharge it.

measuredPopulation.howMeasured: Text extraction of each delivered canonical, reading the line context around the date. rcap-tx-custom-pleading was independently confirmed clean by pixel measurement: the signature-date rect went 829 dark pixels to 0, against a control rect that went 9 to 1,225.
measuredPopulation.note: tx_exp_acquittal-set was returned PASS by RV-A under the narrower reading and is demoted by this determination, not by any new measurement.

determinations.question: How is a missing required component detected when a surviving component occupies its ordinal?
determinations.answer: By name against the registry. Never by ordinal.
determinations.whyOrdinalsCannotSeeIt: West Virginia and Mississippi have the same shape: the registry declares five components ending attachment-4 and instructions-5; the packet renders four and names the fourth filing-instructions-4. The ordinals then read 1,2,3,4 -- unique and contiguous -- and look complete while attachment-4 is absent. Contiguous ordinals are what the collision PRODUCES, so a contiguity check is a test of the symptom's disguise.
determinations.captainErrorRecorded: I first swept the corpus for ordinals that are not 1..n unique-contiguous and found one family. That sweep was measuring the wrong thing and its low count is not evidence of a small population. The name-based sweep is the one that answers this and has not yet been run.
determinations.whatIsMissingWhenItHappens: Not a formatting detail. In Mississippi the absent component is the records checklist carrying 12 participantFilingRequirements across three tracks, and none of the 26 delivered pages carries them.
determinations.consequence: COMPONENT_SET is scored by comparing rendered component names to the registry packetSet's declared names. A corpus-wide name-based sweep is owed.
